name: Wiplink – An MCP and Design System for Divi 5
author: The Imperfect Mind

sections.description:
Wiplink is the free edition of Divi Connect. It links your AI to your Divi 5 website through a secure connector, so you can design and publish real Divi pages just by chatting.

It works with Claude (claude.ai and Desktop), Claude Code, ChatGPT (developer mode), Codex, Gemini CLI and Antigravity, and any other MCP app such as Cursor, Cline or Zed. Pick yours on the Connection screen and it shows you the exact steps for that app.

Every release is listed at divilove.com/changelog.

Your AI reads your site’s actual design system – global colors, font and gradient variables, and module presets – and builds pages that use your tokens, on-brand, then publishes them live. No copy-pasting JSON, no leaving the conversation.

How it works

Wiplink gives your AI the tools to build on your site, and the free Divi 5 Skill – which teaches it how to write valid, on-brand Divi 5 – is built into the connector, so there is nothing extra to install. It loads automatically on connection.

  1. Install Wiplink and copy your connector URL from Wiplink → Connection.
  2. Choose your app on that screen and follow the steps shown for it.
  3. Ask it to build a page – it reads your design system, plans the layout, and publishes it to your site.

Free features

  • Build and publish Divi 5 pages with any supported AI app
  • Read your design system (colors, font and gradient variables, presets)
  • Read your site’s real Divi module schema so pages are built with the correct settings, not guesses
  • Use your color and gradient variables on-brand in generated pages
  • Delete pages
  • Works with claude.ai (free accounts too), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and other MCP apps

The Professional plugin

Divi Connect Professional is a separate plugin. It adds:

  • Writing to your design system from the chat – your AI can create and edit colors, variables and presets
  • The size scale – a fluid spacing and type scale your pages stay linked to, and a screen that reconnects older pages to it
  • Theme Builder templates (headers, footers, post templates)
  • Global layouts and WooCommerce cart and checkout pages
  • Figma import, project memory, Design DNA and flavour export/import
  • Menus and site settings – your AI builds navigation menus and sets the homepage, site title and tagline
  • Multisite networks – this plugin runs on single WordPress sites

Documentation

A complete setup and usage guide – installing, connecting your AI, building pages and troubleshooting – is available at divilove.com.

Translating

Every admin screen of the plugin can be translated. What your AI reads – the connector’s tool descriptions, the built-in Divi 5 Skill – stays in English on purpose, so the AI behaves the same in every language.

  • Once the plugin is listed, translations are made on translate.wordpress.org and arrive on your site as ordinary language packs, with nothing to install.
  • Until then, or to work offline, the template file ships in the plugin’s languages/ folder (the .pot file); open it in Poedit or Loco Translate, save the .po/.mo pair for your locale next to it, and WordPress picks it up.

External services

Wiplink is an interface to an AI assistant that you already use. The plugin itself does not send your content to any AI service. Your AI app connects to your site (over the connector URL and key shown on the Connection screen) and reads or writes only what you ask it to; that traffic is governed by the terms of the AI app you connect – for example Anthropic’s for Claude, OpenAI’s for ChatGPT and Codex, or Google’s for Gemini – and you can close that door at any time with the AI access switch on the Home screen.

The plugin makes outbound requests of its own in these cases only:

  • Draft pictures – by default nothing is sent anywhere: the AI’s page draft is photographed in your own browser, automatically while a Wiplink screen is open, or with one button on Home.
  • The layout library – the free catalog of ready-made sections is fetched from our own server, divilove.com, when you open the Layouts screen or your AI lists layouts (the same files are published in a public GitHub repository). Only the catalog files are requested; nothing about your site is sent beyond the plugin version in the request’s user-agent string. Divi Love’s terms of service and privacy policy apply.
  • Sign in with WordPress, when an app identifies itself by address – some AI apps (Claude, for one) identify themselves with a web address that holds their sign-in details, a Client ID Metadata Document. When such an app connects, this site fetches that one small JSON file from the app maker’s server, checks it, and keeps it for up to a day. Nothing about your site is sent.
  • Images your AI adds by URL – when your AI builds a page with a picture at a web address, the plugin downloads that file into your media library. Only the address you gave it is fetched.
  • A reference page your AI imports – when you ask your AI to use a web page as a reference, the plugin fetches that one address once, reads its structure and text, and stores nothing from it on any other server. Only the address you named is fetched.
  • Google Fonts, on the Design screen – the font picker and the flavour canvas load a font family from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) so you can see it before choosing. Your browser makes that request when you open the picker or preview a flavour; the plugin sends nothing else (Google terms, privacy policy).
  • A help video thumbnail on Home – the Home screen shows the cover image of a short YouTube walkthrough, loaded by your browser from i.ytimg.com, which sets no cookies; the video itself plays only when you press it (YouTube terms, privacy policy).

Divi is a registered trademark of Elegant Themes, Inc. This plugin is not affiliated with nor endorsed by Elegant Themes. Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini and other AI product names are trademarks of their respective owners; this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin’s folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Wiplink → Connection and copy your connector URL.
  4. Choose your app on that screen – Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini CLI and Antigravity, or any other MCP app – then choose how it signs in: Sign in with WordPress (each person gets their own connection, ended from the same screen) or the connector key (one shared key inside the address). The exact steps for that app and that route appear below your choice.
  5. Every sign-in shows up under Connected now on the same screen, with a Sign out button beside it. Ending one connection signs that app out and leaves the others working.

If your AI offers a choice of OAuth client when you add the connector, either works: the option that reads the app maker’s hosted client details (Claude recommends this one) or the option that registers a client automatically. Both end in the same Allow screen.
5. Start a chat and ask for a Divi page. The Divi 5 Skill is built into the connector, so your AI already knows how to write valid, on-brand Divi 5 – there is nothing else to install.

Requires the Divi 5 builder (Divi 5.7 or later).
sections.faq:
Which AI apps does it work with?

Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop), Claude Code, ChatGPT in developer mode, Codex, Gemini CLI and Antigravity, and any other app that speaks MCP – Cursor, Cline and Zed among them. The Connection screen has a panel for each with its own setup steps.

Do I need to install the Divi 5 Skill separately?

No. Since version 1.7.0 the Divi 5 Skill is built into the connector – your AI loads it automatically when it connects, and it always matches your plugin version. There is nothing extra to install, and it works everywhere, including free claude.ai accounts.

The Skill is also published on its own at divilove.com as a free, open-source download. That is optional – useful if you want it loaded in your client for work outside this plugin.

Does it work with a free Claude account?

Yes. Free claude.ai accounts can add the connector and build pages.

Does my site need to be publicly reachable?

For cloud apps such as claude.ai and ChatGPT, yes – the connector URL must be reachable over HTTPS. For apps running on your own machine, such as Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI, a local site works too.

Is it secure?

Each site has its own secret connector key, shown in Settings → Wiplink. You can regenerate it at any time, which instantly invalidates the old one.

What can a connected AI do on my site?

It acts as its own WordPress user, with its own limited role – never as an administrator. You create that user with one click on the Connection screen. It can create, edit and delete pages, posts and projects, add images to the media library, and change your Divi design settings (colours, fonts, presets). It cannot install or change plugins or themes, manage users, change WordPress settings such as the site title, homepage or menus, edit files, or store scripts, stylesheets or custom CSS in a page. Switch AI access off on the Home screen, or delete the AI user on the Users screen, at any time.

Does it work on WordPress Multisite?

No. This plugin runs on single WordPress sites; on a multisite network it does not load and says so on the Plugins screen.

Does it require Divi 5?

Yes. Wiplink targets the Divi 5 builder (5.7+).

Can I use it in my language?

Yes. The admin screens are fully translatable: once the plugin is listed, translations come from translate.wordpress.org as language packs, and the .pot template in the plugin’s languages/ folder lets you translate it yourself in the meantime. What the AI reads stays in English so it behaves the same everywhere.
sections.changelog:
2.4.1

  • New: a Style Guide card on Design › Overview. One click builds a page that shows your colours and fonts.
  • Fixed: after a rollback, updating again clears the “rolled back” notice. It could stay and name the new
    version as the one rolled back to.

2.4.0

A new dashboard. Every Wiplink screen has been rebuilt and rewritten in plain words. Your connection, your pages
and your design stay as they are when you update.

  • New: one menu item per job: Home, Connect AI, Design, Library, History & Activity, and Help & settings.
    Home shows the next step for your site.
  • New: Design has five tabs: Overview, Your choices, Colours & sizes, Health and History. Overview shows how
    your colours, sizes and fonts fit together.
  • New: History & Activity keeps a copy of every page before it changes, your design’s history, and an
    activity log that names the person, or the AI, behind each change.
  • New: the admin screens can be translated.
  • New: the Divi 5 Skill v0.7.3 is built in: Divi 5.12–5.16 additions, Components and Slots.
  • Changed: pages your AI builds stay on your palette. A colour given by name is checked as that colour, a
    text colour your AI chose is kept, and a transparent background no longer counts as dark.
  • Changed: the layout library has more ready-made sections, and every form in it is a real Divi form.
  • Changed: Help & settings opens at once; the connection test runs after the page appears.
  • Changed: the ChatGPT steps on Connect AI follow ChatGPT’s current screens.
  • Changed: stricter permission checks. Every route checks its permission when it is called, and touches only
    posts the connected user may edit.
  • Fixed: a gradient laid over a photo now shows on Divi 5.18.

2.3.6

  • Fixed: ChatGPT can sign in with WordPress again. ChatGPT changed how it identifies itself
    when it signs in to a site, and the sign-in stopped with “This client could not be identified”.
  • Fixed: Sign in with WordPress now works on hosts that answer every /.well-known/ address
    themselves    , such as SiteGround, and the connector answers on sites set to Plain permalinks.
  • Improved: Check the connection tells you when a firewall in front of your site blocks the
    sign-in check    , and points you to the connector key, which still works.
  • Changed: the ChatGPT steps on the Connection screen follow ChatGPT’s current screens.

2.3.4

  • First release in the WordPress.org plugin directory.
